operator_io_quirks: All table/column names are backtick-quoted in DDL; mixed case (Customers, Order_Items, Financial_Transactions) — must preserve original spelling and double-quote in generated SQL.
Tiny DB: every table has exactly 15 rows (Product_Categories 4); original_values sampling of 5 with replacement is a large fraction of the table.

DATETIME columns store TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (space separator, no T, no fractional seconds); declared DATETIME dispatches to Date|Number(int elements) — first element is not int so Date fuzzer with template %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.
Financial_Transactions and Invoice_Line_Items have NO primary key (pk=[]); sample_fresh_primary_keys must be a no-op there, and drop_unique_duplicates has no unique columns to act on.
Products.parent_product_id is an INTEGER that looks like a self-reference to Products.product_id but is NOT declared as an FK — TS will treat it as a plain Number column, not a consistent FK.
Financial_Transactions.transaction_id is INTEGER NOT NULL but not PK and not unique-declared; distinct=15 so effectively unique in original but TS may duplicate.

VARCHAR columns holding numeric-looking strings: product_quantity ('6','7','4'), account_name ('900','520'), gender ('1','0'), customer_middle_initial single letters — String fuzzer will produce arbitrary charset strings, not these shapes.
DECIMAL(19,4) columns store REAL (float) storage class; derived_product_cost/derived_total_cost mix real and integer storage — Number fuzzer with scale=19, precision=4 gives huge ranges.

Several VARCHAR(255) columns are 100% NULL (order_details, transaction_comment, other_transaction_details, other_order_item_details, derived_vat_payable) — distinct=0, samples empty; String sampler with no elements sets p=1 (always fresh).
product_title has distinct=1, value 'prod_name' — a placeholder string, not a real title; TS will treat it as a String with one element.
country has distinct=1 ('USA'); state_county_province distinct=14; town_city distinct=15 — low-cardinality String columns where TS fresh draws will destroy the near-constant distribution.

FK chain depth: Customers -> Orders -> Invoices -> Financial_Transactions and Customers -> Accounts -> Financial_Transactions; Products -> Product_Categories; Order_Items -> Orders, Products; Invoice_Line_Items -> Order_Items, Invoices, Products. All parents exist and are unique on their PK.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on date_order_placed/invoice_date/date_account_opened/transaction_date: template %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S, range from min/max of 5 sampled originals (e.g. 2012..2018), so fresh dates cluster in that window — plausible but narrow; misses queries filtering outside the sampled window.

Number fuzzer on INTEGER PKs: scale=0, range [-1,1] plus perturbation +-1/+-2 — PKs will be tiny ints (0,1,2,-1) and collide heavily; sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicates so tables shrink below requested size.

Number fuzzer on DECIMAL(19,4): scale=19, precision=4, range [-10^19, 10^19] — unit_price, transaction_amount, product_price, vat_rating get astronomically large floats, implausible for money; drives FN on range predicates like unit_price < 1000.

String fuzzer on VARCHAR(50)/(255): charset a-zA-Z 0-9() with length up to declared length (or 20 default) — names, emails, phone numbers, login_password all become random gibberish; LIKE '%@example.com' or phone-pattern queries get FN.
String fuzzer on VARCHAR(1) (gender, customer_middle_initial): length range [0,2) so mostly 1-char random strings, not '0'/'1' or 'A'-'Z' — gender='1' predicates get FN.
String fuzzer on product_quantity VARCHAR(50) holding '6','7': int-like strings get str(i+1), str(i-1) added, so '5','6','7','8' appear — some plausibility preserved; but fresh draws are random.

FK columns (customer_id, order_id, product_id, invoice_number, account_id, order_item_id, production_type_code) draw from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement — ties/duplicates created, so COUNT(DISTINCT) and join-cardinality queries see different multiplicities than original (FP on exact-count queries).
Financial_Transactions and Invoice_Line_Items have no PK: no dedup, so duplicate rows accumulate; COUNT(*) queries get inflated counts (FP).

Product_Categories has only 4 rows and production_type_code is its PK (String): TS may generate 1-30 rows with random strings, breaking the 4-category enum; queries like production_type_code='Books' get FN.
Products.parent_product_id is not an FK: TS generates random Numbers, so self-join Products p1 JOIN Products p2 ON p1.parent_product_id=p2.product_id rarely matches — FN on hierarchy queries.

Low-cardinality String columns (country='USA', transaction_type in {Payment,Refund}, product_color in {Red,Yellow,Black}, product_size in {Small,Medium,Large}, other_account_details in {Regular,VIP}) get random fresh strings — equality predicates on these enums get FN.

NOT NULL columns (customer_id, order_id, date_order_placed, production_type_code, transaction_type, transaction_id, account_id, invoice_number, product_id, order_item_id) may receive NULL from String/Number samplers; insert fails and row is skipped, shrinking tables further.
